name: Whirlpool
label: Revelation
lede: Two guys who worked at Revelation wanted a Pixies-style boy-girl band, got two records out of it, and then lost their drummer and guitarist to Sense Field's Warner Bros. deal.

eras.title: A side project from the Revelation warehouse
eras.text: Rodney Sellars had more songs than Sense Field could use, and a co-worker at Revelation, Travis Guichard of Mean Season and Outspoken, had a house to jam in. Sellars was deep into the Pixies and wanted a man and a woman singing together.

years.h: Rodney Sellars and Travis Guichard start Whirlpool
years.p: Sense Field guitarist Rodney Sellars and Travis Guichard meet working at Revelation Records and jam at Guichard's house twice a week. They add the Laws brothers, Travis on bass and Brandon on drums, and singer Rachel Stolte.
years.xp: Travis Laws was one of Sellars's roommates and had played bass in [[Final Conflict|dc6848f9-0eda-4981-b5ca-f113d9658c2e]] for years, so he was, in Guichard's words, an easy fix. Sellars wanted a male/female vocal blend like the Pixies, which is how Stolte came in.

years.p: Whirlpool's first album comes out on Revelation. The first press: 2,984 on black vinyl and 305 on green.

Whirlpool make one US tour, in summer 1995. Travis Guichard says it helped to share bills with bands like [[Iceburn|b3aa7443-5572-4c1f-99e5-a91e13cd3e5b]], [[Engine Kid|899baef6-af48-4caa-aff6-c1562a5dc12d]], [[Deadguy|311e7afe-e0e3-476a-a703-fcd61dc049ac]], [[Shades Apart|3f6c4af4-bb50-4672-998e-5e806b696fb3]], [[Braid|12269eae-3c21-4586-acf2-6cb03c92f4e7]] and [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]].

years.h: Whirlpool fly to New York for CMJ at CBGB
years.p: Whirlpool's one East Coast trip: a CMJ Music Marathon showcase at CBGB in September 1995.

eras.title: The most Revelation ever spent on studio time
eras.text: Revelation bet on Whirlpool's second record more than it had on any LP before. Then Sense Field signed to Warner Bros., and Whirlpool shared two of its members with Sense Field.

years.h: Scott McPherson of Sense Field takes over Whirlpool's drums
years.p: [[Scott McPherson|c857aba4-942d-448c-b172-7807647c648d]], Rodney Sellars's bandmate in Sense Field, plays drums on Whirlpool's second album in place of Brandon Laws.

q: We had a great relationship with Jordan Cooper and Revelation.
years.src: No Echo · Discogs · RevHQ · Revelation Records pressing history
years.p: Produced by Jim Monroe and the band at For The Record. Travis Guichard believes it was the most money Revelation had ever spent on studio time for an LP.
years.xp:
Twelve songs, including Machine Religion, Wasteland, Deutchland and one called Cindy Crawford Pumpkin. Ed Kampworth adds keyboards on some tracks. Revelation pitched it to fans of the Pixies and X.

A second press included 110 copies on blue vinyl.

years.big: Warner signed Sense Field. Whirlpool paid for it.
years.src: No Echo: Travis Guichard · Wikipedia: Sense Field
years.h: Sense Field's Warner Bros. deal ends Whirlpool
years.p: Sense Field sign with Warner Bros. in 1996, and Scott McPherson and Rodney Sellars can't do both. Travis Guichard says Whirlpool just couldn't continue, and he was at peace with it.
years.xp: It was mutual, and nobody fell out. The members stayed friends and kept playing together off and on. Warner then left Sense Field in limbo for five years.

eras.title: Back in Rodney's garage
eras.text: Nearly two decades later, two Whirlpool founders ended up under one roof again.

years.h: Travis Guichard moves in with Rodney Sellars
years.p: Back in the US after years in Europe, Travis Guichard lives at Rodney Sellars's house and spends most of his time in the garage writing and recording. None of it has been released.
